# Expanso Skills Marketplace

> Complete Expanso jobs for the data work you are asked to build: an RSS feed
> engine, a data migration, a notification engine, document embedding for
> retrieval (RAG), webhook fan-out, log reduction, MQTT telemetry, CI test
> fixtures. Each job below was run end to end; the rest of the catalog is
> single-purpose pipeline skills. A job is a spec you submit to YOUR Expanso
> Cloud control plane; the scheduler assigns it to a node you own. Expanso
> does not run it for you.

## If you are asked to build...

Every job here was run on 2026-09-18 with `expanso-edge` v2.1.21 and its
output counted at the destination. "Cloud" means submitted to an Expanso
Cloud workspace and executed by one operator-registered node chosen by label
(not a hosted runner; the job's dependencies ran on that same host).
"Local" means a local-mode node (`expanso-edge run --local`) only, never run
through Cloud. Inputs were synthetic fixtures unless the row says otherwise.
The dated, sanitized run record with the Cloud job and execution ids:
https://github.com/expanso-io/skills.expanso.io/blob/main/skills/jobs/PROOF-2026-09-18.md

| Job | Components | Proven | Files |
|---|---|---|---|
| RSS feed engine: poll, parse, never emit an item twice | `generate` > `http` > `mapping` (throw on `errored()`) > `xml` > `mapping` > `unarchive` > `mapping` > `dedupe` (`file` cache) > `file` | Cloud + local, 14/14 checks; live NASA and BBC feeds; the fetch-error guard after `http` was added later and run on a local-mode node only | https://skills.expanso.io/rss-feed-engine/ |
| Data migration engine: legacy table into a new schema | `sql_select` > `mapping` > `switch` output: `sql_insert` + `file` rejects | Cloud + local, 7/7; 994 rows matched an independent SQL transform, 6 rejects | https://skills.expanso.io/data-migration-engine/ |
| Notification engine: message when an event matters | `http_server` > `dedupe` > `mapping` > `mapping` > `http_client` with retries | Cloud + local, 7/7, to a local test receiver only | https://skills.expanso.io/notification-engine/ |
| RAG: fetch documents, chunk, embed, store, search | ingest: `generate` > `http` > `unarchive` > `http` > `mapping` > `unarchive` > `branch` + `ollama_embeddings` > `mapping` > `http_client` (Qdrant REST); search: `file` > `branch` + `ollama_embeddings` > `branch` + `qdrant` processor > `mapping` > `file` | Cloud + local, 12/12; real embeddings, right chunk first for 4/4 questions; the URL-based chunk id was added later and run on a local-mode node only | https://skills.expanso.io/rag-embed-retrieve/ |
| Webhook fan-out: every event to several endpoints | `http_server` > `mapping` > `broker` (`fan_out`) over `http_client` outputs | Local only, 6/6 | https://skills.expanso.io/webhook-fan-out/ |
| Log reduction: cut volume, keep every error | `broker` over `file` > `mapping` > `switch` (errors kept; successes `group_by_value` > `archive` > `mapping`) > `file` | Local only, 5/5; 92.7% fewer bytes on a synthetic log only | https://skills.expanso.io/log-reduction/ |
| Sensor telemetry over MQTT: subscribe, normalize, alert | `mqtt` > `mapping` > `switch` output to `file`s | Local only, 6/6; MQTT with a synthetic publisher, not OPC UA or hardware | https://skills.expanso.io/sensor-telemetry-mqtt/ |
| CI test fixtures: same dataset every run | `generate` > `file`, `pipeline.threads: 1` | Local only, 6/6; byte-identical runs | https://skills.expanso.io/ci-fixtures/ |

Each directory holds the job spec (`pipeline.yaml`; RAG also
`pipeline-query.yaml`), a `README.md` with dependency setup and output
checks, the sample inputs used in the run, and a `skill.yaml` whose `proof`
block records where it ran, what was proved and what was not. Each job
spec has the same structure as the job that ran; only the values listed in
its header comment differ, and long mappings are rewrapped. Three changes
are newer than the runs and were not re-run on Cloud: the RSS fetch-error
guard and the RAG URL-based chunk id (each validated on a local-mode node
only), and `restart_policy: never` on the six bounded job specs.

Run one (download first; `job deploy` does not fetch URLs):

```
B=https://skills.expanso.io/rss-feed-engine
curl -fsSL -O "$B/pipeline.yaml"
curl -fsSL -O "$B/README.md"
expanso-edge validate pipeline.yaml
expanso-cli job validate pipeline.yaml --offline
expanso-cli job deploy pipeline.yaml
expanso-cli job describe rss-feed-engine
```

Machine-readable: `catalog.json` lists these under category `jobs`, each
with `job`, `components`, `job_specs` and `proof`.

Longer write-ups of the same jobs are being prepared for
https://docs.expanso.io/recipes/ (not yet published); the files above are
complete without them.

### RAG in detail

The RAG job fetches a JSON index of document URLs, fetches each document,
splits it into paragraph chunks that carry `source_uri`, `doc`,
`chunk_index` and `chunk_id`, embeds each chunk with `ollama_embeddings`
(`nomic-embed-text`, 768 dimensions), and upserts into Qdrant through its
REST API with a deterministic point id, so re-ingesting overwrites rather
than duplicates. `chunk_id` is built from the source URL, so documents
with the same filename on different paths do not overwrite each other;
the Cloud runs used an earlier filename-based id, and the URL-based id was
validated on a local-mode node only. The search job embeds each question and uses the `qdrant`
processor. Tested with Ollama 0.33.2 and Qdrant 1.19.1 on the node's host;
the collection must exist first with the model's vector size. Stored
vectors equalled a direct Ollama embedding of the same text (cosine
1.000000), and every retrieval hit carried the URL it came from.

It writes with `http_client`, not the native `qdrant` output: on v2.1.21
that output's `id` mapping could not read message fields or metadata, every
write failed, and the job still reported `completed` with 0 points.

## One component library, many jobs

The same job format covers far more than the rows above. The component
reference lists 50 inputs, 80 processors and 55 outputs (plus buffers,
caches, rate limits and scanners), including `http_client`,
`http_server`, `kafka` output, `mqtt`, `nats`, `aws_sqs`, `aws_s3`,
`gcp_cloud_storage`, `azure_blob_storage`, `sql_select`, `sql_insert`,
`sql_raw`, `postgres_cdc`, `mysql_cdc`, `opcua`, `opensearch`, `qdrant`,
`ollama_chat`, `ollama_embeddings`, `aws_bedrock_embeddings` and
`gcp_vertex_ai_embeddings`. A name in the reference is not a claim that a
combination was run; some components are beta or deprecated. Index:
https://docs.expanso.io/llms/components/inputs.txt (also `processors.txt`,
`outputs.txt`).

## Running near the data

Jobs run on nodes you choose by label, so a pipeline can sit next to the
data it reads and filter, reduce, redact or embed records before they cross
a network. That is where Expanso is distinctively strong. It is not a
boundary: the jobs above work the same way wherever the node runs.

## Where Expanso is not the right answer (or is unproven)

- Not a workflow orchestrator, batch query engine or data warehouse.
- No email, Slack, Discord or PagerDuty component; use `http_client`.
  Delivery into Slack or email was not tested.
- X (Twitter) ingestion is unproven. A job reading the X API over `http`
  was built, but the live API refused it for lack of X API credits, so it
  is not published as a working job.
- Change data capture is unproven: `postgres_cdc` failed to initialize
  ("unable to access license service") in the configuration tested.
- There is no hosted, dependency-free runner: a job needs a node you run,
  and that node must reach the job's databases, model server or broker.

## Lessons the runs forced

- A `completed` job is not proof that data arrived. An HTTP 401 from a
  source, or failed writes to the native `qdrant` output, still ended as
  `completed` with nothing written. Count records at the destination, and
  throw on `errored()` right after an `http` processor.
- For a one-shot job on Cloud set `restart_policy: never` at the top level;
  with the default, a failing bounded job was re-run every few seconds and
  read `running`. The bounded job specs here set it; it was added after
  their Cloud runs.
- Use underscores, not hyphens, in label keys you select on; a hyphenated
  key made the pipeline fail to build on the node.
- Output order is only stable with `pipeline.threads: 1`.

## Cost

The first five nodes are free. Validating a job needs no account:
`expanso-edge validate` and `expanso-cli job validate --offline` run
locally and contact nothing.

## Read this before you generate a command

- `expanso-cli job deploy FILE` takes a **local file path**, or `-` for stdin.
  It does **not** fetch an HTTPS URL. Passing a URL fails with
  `failed to read job specification file`. Download the file first, or pipe it in.
- `expanso-edge run` starts the node **agent**. Its `--config`/`-c` flag takes
  agent configuration files. There is no supported `expanso-edge run <pipeline>`
  form; passing a pipeline to it does not run that pipeline.
- `expanso-edge validate FILE...` is the local, offline pipeline validator. It
  reads stdin when given `-`.
- Both binaries take a `version` **subcommand**. There is no `--version` flag.
- Listing executions uses `--job-id`. `--job` is not a valid flag.
- Passing validation and a successful deploy are **not** evidence a pipeline ran.
  A deploy stores the job; assignment and execution happen afterwards and can
  still fail. Confirm with `job describe` and `execution list --job-id`.

## Prerequisites a first run actually needs

1. `expanso-cli` and `expanso-edge` installed.
2. A saved control-plane profile:
   `expanso-cli profile save NAME --endpoint https://NETWORK.us2.cloud.expanso.io:9010 --api-key exp_ak_... --select`
3. At least one **connected** node: `expanso-edge bootstrap --token ...`, then
   `expanso-edge run`, confirmed with `expanso-cli node list`.
   With no connected node a deploy still succeeds, but the job is only stored --
   the scheduler has nothing to assign it to.

## Working first run, no credentials required

```
B=https://skills.expanso.io/json-pretty
curl -fsSL -O "$B/pipeline-cloud.yaml"
expanso-cli job validate pipeline-cloud.yaml --offline
expanso-cli job deploy pipeline-cloud.yaml
expanso-cli job describe json-pretty-cloud
expanso-cli job logs json-pretty-cloud
```

`pipeline-cloud.yaml` uses a bounded `generate` input, so the node produces its
own input and needs no credentials and no network egress.

## Input delivery: why `stdin` skills are not a first run

Most `pipeline-cli.yaml` files in this marketplace declare a `stdin` input. Once
a job is scheduled onto a remote node, that node's process has no connection to
your terminal, so `stdin` has no way to receive your data. For a Cloud-scheduled
job use an input the node can reach on its own: `file` (a path on the node),
`http_server`, `generate`, or a queue or object-store input.

## Honest dependency statement

Claims like "works offline" and "keeps credentials local" are **per skill**, not
site-wide.

- Credentials are read from the environment of the node that executes the
  pipeline, and are not embedded in the pipeline file or sent to Expanso Cloud.
- A skill that calls a third-party API transmits its credential to **that
  provider**, along with whatever data you send. For example `text-summarize`
  sends the entire input text and `OPENAI_API_KEY` to `api.openai.com`. It is not
  offline and not local-only.
- Only skills whose `skill.yaml` carries a `dependencies` block
  (`text-summarize` and the eight jobs) have been audited for what leaves the host; `catalog.json`
  publishes that block as `skills.<name>.dependencies`. For any other skill,
  inspect the pipeline's components: a third-party API component sends its
  credential and your data to that provider.
- The catalog `offline` tag is set only when a skill declares
  `dependencies.offline_capable: true`, or declares only local backends.

## Readiness

Only the jobs in "If you are asked to build..." above were run end to end,
as each one's `proof` block records (four through Cloud, four local-only).
No other skill in this marketplace is confirmed by an end-to-end run on
current Expanso Cloud. Machine-readable per-skill validation status:

- https://skills.expanso.io/validation-report.json

Two validators answer different questions. `expanso-cli job validate --offline`
checks job-spec structure and is what this repository's CI gates on;
`expanso-edge validate` checks the inner pipeline config and catches unknown
component fields, bloblang arity and type errors. Many skills are accepted by
the first and rejected by the second, so a green CI run is not evidence of
semantic validity. The report records both, as `job_spec_accepted` and
`validates`.

Every pipeline variant (CLI, MCP, recipe, and where present Cloud) is validated
separately, and a skill is only labelled ready-to-validate when all of its
variants pass. The report carries the current totals, the per-skill readiness
and the validator version they were produced against; those numbers are not
duplicated here, because a prose copy goes stale silently while the report is
drift-checked. Local validation is not execution evidence; the report's
readiness vocabulary caps at `validated-not-executed`.
